directAnswer: To show hidden files on a Mac, you can use a keyboard shortcut in Finder or modify Terminal settings.
summary: This guide explains how to reveal hidden files on macOS using keyboard shortcuts or Terminal commands.

sections.heading: Using Keyboard Shortcut
sections.body: In Finder, you can quickly toggle the visibility of hidden files by pressing Command + Shift + Period (⌘ + ⇧ + .). This method works in most recent versions of macOS.

sections.heading: Using Terminal
sections.body: If you prefer using Terminal, you can show hidden files by entering the command: 'defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles true' followed by 'killall Finder' to refresh Finder.

steps.title: Show Hidden Files with Shortcut
steps.detail: Open any Finder window and press Command + Shift + Period (⌘ + ⇧ + .) to toggle hidden files.

steps.title: Show Hidden Files with Terminal
steps.detail: Open Terminal and run 'defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles true', then type 'killall Finder' to apply changes.

faqs.question: How do I revert back to hiding files?
faqs.answer: You can revert back by using the same keyboard shortcut (Command + Shift + Period) or by running 'defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles false' in Terminal followed by 'killall Finder'.

faqs.question: Will this affect all applications?
faqs.answer: No, this change only affects Finder. Other applications may have their own settings for showing hidden files.

faqs.question: Are there any risks in showing hidden files?
faqs.answer: Yes, hidden files often contain system or application data. Modifying or deleting them can cause issues with system functionality.

caveats: The keyboard shortcut may not work in older versions of macOS, where Terminal commands are recommended.
